newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian forces kill 88 Moslem rebels - paper.
newsitem.headline: Algerian forces kill 88 Moslem rebels - paper.

text.p: Algerian security forces have killed 88 Moslem guerrillas over the past week in operations carried out in four rebel strongholds, a leading Algerian newspaper said on Sunday.
At least 18 other rebels were killed in infighting between guerrilla factions, said El Watan daily, quoting what it called a reliable sources.
Security forces, in a simultaneous operations in Medea and the mountainous Chrea regions, killed 60 guerrillas, it said.

More than 150 villagers had been slaughtered in the past four months in Chrea and Medea in suspected Moslem guerrilla raids, including 33 people hacked to death 10 days ago in Kerrach hamlet in Chrea area, 50 km (30 miles) south of Algiers.
Twenty-three guerrillas were killed on Thursday and Friday in Magtaa Kheira village, 60 km (40 miles) southwest of Algiers, said El Watan widely seen as well-informed in security affairs.
Security forces stormed a rebel hideout in Algiers last week killing five guerrillas holding a meeting to plot unspecified attacks in the Algerian capital, the paper added.
The paper made no mention of casualties in the ranks of the security forces.
The bodies of five guerrillas killed in infighting were found on Thursday on a road side in Larba, 22 km (13 miles) south of Algiers, El Watan said.
The five men were members of a group which broke away with the Armed Islamic Group (GIA), Algeria's ruthless guerrilla faction, it said.
Thirteen more guerrillas have died in the past week in a turf war between rival guerrilla factions in the western region of Sidi Bel Abbes, El Watan added.
President Liamine Zeroual was quoted earlier this month as saying that the latest wave of killing in Algeria was the result of settling scores between rival Moslem rebels.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
The government plans to hold multiparty parliamentary elections on May 29 or June 5.
